heroes.label: Sword & Shield Fighter
heroes.blurb: A veteran sergeant in heavy mail who stands in the doorway and holds it, so the rest of you can do something clever.

character.name: Marta Strom
traits: Counts everything out loud — arrows, paces, rations, days
Steps in front of people before deciding whether they deserve it
Does not trust cavalry, or anyone who has never stood a night watch
Sleeps in her armour and sees no reason to apologise for it

features.name: Fighting Style: Dueling
features.description: +2 damage with a one-handed melee weapon when nothing else is in her other hand but a shield. Longsword: +5 to hit, 1d8+5 slashing (1d10+5 with both hands).

features.name: Second Wind
features.description: Once per short rest, as a bonus action, regain 1d10+1 hit points.

features.name: Savage Attacker (Human feat)
features.description: Once per turn when she rolls damage for a melee weapon, she may reroll the damage dice and use either total.

features.name: Handaxe
features.description: +5 to hit, 1d6+3 slashing, thrown 20/60 ft — the answer to anything that will not come to her.

features.name: Shield Wall Discipline
features.description: Trained to hold a line: she fights shoulder to shoulder, takes the first hit, and gives the party a round to get organised.

character.gear: Chain Mail · Shield · Longsword · Handaxe · Bedroll · Field Rations · Whetstone · Torn Muster Roll
character.story: Marta Strom spent eleven years holding other people's lines. She was a sergeant of the shield wall at Kalder Ford, where the company was told to hold for one day and held for six; by the end there were nine of them and a great deal of mud. She mustered out with her armour, her pay in arrears, and a roster of names to deliver to families who had already stopped expecting anyone. That took a year. Now she hires out to whoever is standing between something and someone, and she is careful to ask which side of the wall they intend her to be on.

inventory.name: Chain Mail
inventory.lore: Sergeant Voss's spare shirt, re-riveted twice and still carrying a dent below the collarbone where a boar spear got lucky. Marta oils the rings on the same night every week, whether or not there is a war on.
inventory.description: Heavy interlocking rings; slow, loud, and worth every pound.

inventory.name: Shield
inventory.lore: Painted over so many times the old crest is a lump under the paint. She has never scraped it back to see whose it was.
inventory.description: A round wooden shield with an iron boss and a leather grip.

inventory.name: Longsword
inventory.lore: Standard muster issue, straight off the rack, and that is exactly why she trusts it: a sword you did not choose cannot disappoint you.
inventory.description: A straight double-edged blade, well kept and unremarkable.

inventory.name: Handaxe
inventory.lore: Won off a sapper in a card game she should not have played. The haft is scorched where he used it to tap fuses.
inventory.description: A short-hafted axe balanced for throwing.

inventory.name: Bedroll
inventory.lore: Waxed canvas over straw ticking, rolled tight with a strap she cut from a dead man's harness and does not talk about.
inventory.description: A weatherproofed bedroll for cold ground.

inventory.name: Field Rations
inventory.lore: Hard black bread and salted pork from the garrison stores. She eats the bread last because it is the only thing that keeps its shape in the rain.
inventory.description: Five days of marching food.

inventory.name: Whetstone
inventory.lore: A grey river stone worn into a shallow curve over years of the same motion. It belonged to her first sergeant, who gave it away the day he stopped caring about his blade.
inventory.description: A palm-sized sharpening stone.

inventory.name: Torn Muster Roll
inventory.lore: Forty-one names in a clerk's careful hand, with three crossed out and one circled. She carries it folded to the size of a thumb and has never explained the circle.
inventory.description: A fragment of a company roster, soft as cloth from handling.

heroes.label: Sneaky Halfling Rogue
heroes.blurb: A small, cheerful burglar with a shortbow, two daggers and a talent for being somewhere you did not expect.

character.name: Wren Farrow
traits: Pockets first, questions later, apologies never
Talks her way out of trouble she caused on purpose
Keeps a running tally of favours owed, in both directions
Never enters a room without counting the exits and the loose floorboards

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.description: Once per turn, deal an extra 1d6 damage when she has advantage on the attack, or when an ally is within 5 ft of the target and she does not have disadvantage. Shortbow: +5 to hit, 1d6+3 piercing (+1d6 sneak). Dagger: +5 to hit, 1d4+3 piercing.

features.name: Expertise
features.description: Double proficiency on two skills: Stealth +7 and Sleight of Hand +7.

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.description: A secret mix of dialect, jargon and code; she can hide messages in ordinary conversation and read the marks other thieves leave on doors.

features.name: Lucky (Halfling)
features.description: When she rolls a 1 on an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, she may reroll it and must use the new roll.

features.name: Brave (Halfling)
features.description: Advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

features.name: Halfling Nimbleness
features.description: She can move through the space of any creature larger than her.

features.name: Naturally Stealthy (Lightfoot)
features.description: She can attempt to hide even when obscured only by a creature at least one size larger than her.

character.gear: Leather Armor · Shortbow · Quiver of Arrows · Daggers · Thieves' Tools · Hooded Lantern · Loaded Bone Dice · Crooked Brass Key
character.story: Wren Farrow grew up over a stable in Fennick, the smallest of six, and learned early that the surest way to be seen was to be loud and the surest way to be fed was not to be seen at all. By nine she was running errands for a fence called Auntie Pike; by sixteen she was the one other thieves sent up the drainpipes. Then a job went wrong in a way that was not her fault and that nobody believed was not her fault, and Fennick became a place with too many people in it who knew her face. She travels light, owes three debts and pretends to owe none, and is genuinely, inconveniently good company.

inventory.name: Leather Armor
inventory.lore: Cut down from a coachman's coat and restitched by a woman in Fennick who asked no questions and took payment in the shape of a rumour. It still smells faintly of horses and rain.
inventory.description: Supple boiled leather, quiet in the joints.

inventory.name: Shortbow
inventory.lore: A child's hunting bow that grew up with her. The grip is wrapped in the leather of a bootlace she outgrew at fourteen and could not bring herself to throw away.
inventory.description: A short yew bow, drawn fast and carried easy.

inventory.name: Quiver of Arrows
inventory.lore: Twenty shafts, four of them fletched with goose rather than pigeon. The goose ones are for people, and she keeps count of how many she has left.
inventory.description: A plain quiver with twenty arrows.

inventory.name: Daggers
inventory.lore: Mismatched pair — one balanced for throwing, one ground thin for close work. The thin one was a gift, which is the only reason she has not sold it.
inventory.description: Two short blades, one weighted to throw.

inventory.name: Thieves' Tools
inventory.lore: Rolled in oiled cloth: picks, a tension wrench, a tiny saw. Three of the picks she made herself from clock springs, and they are better than the bought ones.
inventory.description: Picks, wrenches and clamps in a soft roll.
properties: proficiency required for locks and traps

inventory.name: Hooded Lantern
inventory.lore: Bought with her first honest payment and dented the same week. She claims the dent improves the light; it does not.
inventory.description: A brass lantern with a sliding shutter.

inventory.name: Loaded Bone Dice
inventory.lore: Two dice that roll how she wants when she wants, and honestly when she is bored. Her father's, and the reason she left home before she was asked to.
inventory.description: A pair of yellowed dice, one heavier on a corner.

inventory.name: Crooked Brass Key
inventory.lore: It opens nothing any more; the door it belonged to was pulled down for firewood a winter ago. She keeps it because a key is a good thing to be holding when someone asks why you are somewhere.
inventory.description: A small bent key on a waxed cord.

heroes.label: Healing Wood-Elf Cleric
heroes.blurb: A shrine healer with a mace and a shield who keeps everyone standing, and takes it personally when she cannot.

character.name: Ailsa Rook
character.background: Cleric · Acolyte (shrine healer of the Green Lady)

spells.name: Sacred Flame
spells.description: Flame-like radiance descends on one creature she can see within 60 feet. The target must succeed on a DEX saving throw (DC 13) or take 1d8 radiant damage. Cover grants no benefit against this spell.

spells.name: Guidance
spells.description: She touches one willing creature and chooses a skill. Once before the spell ends (concentration, up to 1 minute), that creature adds 1d4 to one ability check using that skill.

spells.name: Light
spells.description: She touches an object no larger than 20 feet in any dimension. It sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet, in a colour she chooses. Ends if she casts it again or dismisses it.

spells.name: Bless
spells.description: Up to three creatures within 30 feet add 1d4 to every attack roll and saving throw for 1 minute (concentration). Life Domain spell — always prepared.

spells.name: Cure Wounds
spells.description: She touches a creature and it regains 1d8+3 hit points. With Disciple of Life this heals 1d8+6. Life Domain spell — always prepared.

spells.name: Healing Word
spells.description: A creature she can see within 60 feet regains 1d8+3 hit points. With Disciple of Life this heals 1d8+6. Castable at range, as a bonus action — the reason she is still alive.

spells.name: Shield of Faith
spells.description: A shimmering field surrounds one creature within 60 feet, granting +2 AC for up to 10 minutes (concentration).

traits: Treats every wound as a small argument with death that she intends to win
Talks to trees more easily than to people, and is aware of it
Keeps a mental list of everyone she has failed to save, in order
Refuses to sleep indoors when there is a sky to sleep under

features.name: Spellcasting (Cleric)
features.description: Wisdom is her casting ability: spell save DC 13, spell attack +5. Three cantrips known, four 1st-level spells prepared, two 1st-level slots.

features.name: Divine Domain: Life
features.description: Disciple of Life — whenever a spell of 1st level or higher restores hit points, the target regains an extra 2 + the spell's level. Bless and Cure Wounds are always prepared.

features.name: Mace
features.description: +3 to hit, 1d6+1 bludgeoning — she is not a warrior and has never pretended otherwise.

features.name: Darkvision (Wood Elf)
features.description: She sees in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light.

features.name: Fey Ancestry (Wood Elf)
features.description: Advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put her to sleep.

features.name: Trance (Wood Elf)
features.description: She does not sleep. Four hours of meditation gives the same rest as eight hours of sleep, and she is conscious throughout.

features.name: Keen Senses & Elf Weapon Training
features.description: Proficiency in Perception; proficient with longsword, shortsword, shortbow and longbow.

features.name: Mask of the Wild (Wood Elf)
features.description: She can attempt to hide even when only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist or other natural phenomena.

character.gear: Scale Mail · Shield · Mace · Wooden Holy Symbol · Healer's Kit · Bedroll · Field Rations · Bundle of Dried Yarrow
character.story: Ailsa Rook was left at the shrine of the Green Lady in the year of the long cough, and the shrine kept her because nobody came to claim her. She grew up learning which moss closes a wound and which one only stains the bandage, and she was content to be useful in a small place. Then a fever went through Rook's Reach and she sat with forty people and saved nineteen, and the arithmetic of that has followed her out of the valley. She travels now with a mace she does not like and a healer's kit she does, looking for the difference between a cure and a delay.

inventory.name: Scale Mail
inventory.lore: Temple issue, and older than she is: the scales were re-laid by a smith in Rook's Reach who stamped his mark inside the collar, where the wearer's neck hides it. Two of the scales are bronze, replacements from a season she was not born for.
inventory.description: Overlapping metal scales on a heavy leather coat.

inventory.name: Shield
inventory.lore: Painted with a green shoot coming through a stone — the sign of the shrine where she took her vows. The paint is renewed each spring, badly, by her own hand.
inventory.description: A round shield, painted and scarred.

inventory.name: Mace
inventory.lore: The head is a plain iron ball; the haft is wrapped in cord she replaced herself after the original rotted. She has used it twice in anger and remembers both.
inventory.description: A simple flanged mace, worn smooth at the grip.

inventory.name: Wooden Holy Symbol
inventory.lore: Carved from the heartwood of a tree that fell across the shrine path in a storm and was never cleared. It is warm to the touch for reasons she attributes to faith and the woodcutter attributes to friction.
inventory.description: A palm-sized emblem of a shoot breaking stone.

inventory.name: Healer's Kit
inventory.lore: Linen strips, a bone needle, a clay pot of salve that smells of pine tar. The pot is chipped where she dropped it running, and she has never quite forgiven herself for the waste.
inventory.description: Ten uses of bandages, splints and salve.

inventory.name: Bedroll
inventory.lore: Wool, patched at the foot with a piece of altar cloth too worn to serve. She sleeps better on it than in any bed she has been offered.
inventory.description: A heavy wool bedroll.

inventory.name: Field Rations
inventory.lore: Oat cake, hard cheese, dried apples from the shrine orchard. She shares them badly — which is to say, completely — and then goes hungry with an air of martyrdom.
inventory.description: Four days of plain travelling food.

inventory.name: Bundle of Dried Yarrow
inventory.lore: Cut at midsummer and hung to dry in the shrine rafters. It stops bleeding and it steadies a frightened animal, and she has used it on both more often than on people.
inventory.description: A paper twist of dried yarrow stalks.
